name: Bean, corn and spinach quesadillas
summary: Wholewheat tortillas folded around spiced kidney beans, sweetcorn, spinach and a little cheddar, toasted crisp in a dry pan and served with fresh tomato salsa.
about: Quesadillas come from Mexico, where a tortilla is folded around cheese and heated on a griddle until it melts. Filled mostly with beans and vegetables and only a little cheese, they make a meat-free supper that children can help to fold.

ingredients.name: Spring onions
ingredients.note: sliced, white and green parts kept apart

steps: Mix the tomatoes, red onion, coriander and lemon juice with a pinch of salt in a small bowl and set aside while you make the filling.

Heat the oven to 100 °C to keep the cooked quesadillas warm. Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat, add the red pepper and the white parts of the spring onions and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin and paprika for 30 seconds, then add the beans and sweetcorn. Roughly mash about half the beans against the pan with a fork and cook for 2 minutes, until hot.

Add the spinach a handful at a time and stir for 1–2 minutes, until wilted and the mixture looks thick rather than wet. Stir in the green spring onion, season with salt and tip into a bowl. Wipe the pan clean.
Spread a sixth of the filling over one half of each tortilla, scatter a sixth of the cheddar on top, fold the bare half over and press down gently.

Heat the clean pan over medium heat with no oil. Toast two quesadillas at a time for 2–3 minutes a side, pressing with a spatula, until crisp with golden spots and the cheese has melted. Keep each batch warm in the oven while you cook the rest.
Cut each quesadilla into 3 wedges and serve with the salsa and a salad of lettuce and cucumber.
prepNote: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and keep it in the fridge; fill and toast the tortillas when you need them.
